# pr-1612: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone ## Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
This is a PR rework task. Let me read the input files for pr-1612.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 12 - **Additions**: +1118 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:44:39Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1612._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/spill/spill.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`

# pr-1612: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone ## Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 12 - **Additions**: +1118 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:44:39Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1612._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/spill/spill.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: a command whose first line is empty renders a faceless label**

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc accuracy — "Two guards" lists three bullets, and the third describes behavior that can't happen**

- "Two guards keep the pass sane" is followed by **three** bullets.
- The third bullet ("a trigger at/above the window clamps to `window` (fire at the window, never past it)") describes an unreachable outcome: `clamped = window` always satisfies `clamped >= defaultTrigger`, so that input returns `base` as a no-op two lines earlier — it never "fires at the window". The test correctly pins the no-op; the doc should say "a trigger at/above the default threshold (the window included) is a no-op".

Worth fixing while the file is new — this is the doc bench operators will read to size `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/spill/spill.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: document the preview-bound floor of the env cap**

`resolveRunSpillsConfig` lets an operator set any positive threshold, but the preview bounds stay at the defaults (`headChars + tailChars = 4000`), and `buildPreview` now renders a body that fits those bounds **in full**. So `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=1000` doesn't cap the model-visible output at ~1000 chars — a spilled body of 101–4000 chars still renders whole; the effective worst case is 4000 + header. Fine for gh-1604's "unsanitized 62K-line dumps" target, but the knob's doc ("a positive integer is the spill threshold in chars") reads as a hard cap.

Suggest one sentence on the env var's doc: *"the model-visible preview never exceeds the head+tail bounds (defaults: 4000 chars); thresholds below that floor change when spilling fires, not the preview's worst-case size."*

---

### Thread 7 — `test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: stale numbers in the test header comment**

The header says the default trigger on a 200k window "fires only at 183184" estimated tokens, but `CompactionSettings.forWindow(200000)` gives `reserveTokens = 16384` → trigger = 200000 − 16384 = **183616** (which is what `_defaultTrigger` on line 22 actually computes — the code is right, only the prose numbers are off, in both this line and line 20).

---

**Summary**: One 🚨 BLOCKING bug — `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` throws an uncaught `ArgumentError` from `withCompactionTriggerTokens` (`int.clamp(1, 0)`), which propagates out of every compaction gate (run loop, resume boot cap, resume budget) and kills the run instead of degrading to defaults (reproduced against the packaged API). One ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override, contradicting the PR description, with no test pinning either precedence. Plus five 💡 suggestions (spills notes dropped on env override, faceless label for leading-newline commands, doc nits).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 12 - **Additions**: +1118 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:44:39Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1612._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/spill/spill.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: a command whose first line is empty renders a faceless label**

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc accuracy — "Two guards" lists three bullets, and the third describes behavior that can't happen**

- "Two guards keep the pass sane" is followed by **three** bullets.
- The third bullet ("a trigger at/above the window clamps to `window` (fire at the window, never past it)") describes an unreachable outcome: `clamped = window` always satisfies `clamped >= defaultTrigger`, so that input returns `base` as a no-op two lines earlier — it never "fires at the window". The test correctly pins the no-op; the doc should say "a trigger at/above the default threshold (the window included) is a no-op".

Worth fixing while the file is new — this is the doc bench operators will read to size `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/spill/spill.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: document the preview-bound floor of the env cap**

`resolveRunSpillsConfig` lets an operator set any positive threshold, but the preview bounds stay at the defaults (`headChars + tailChars = 4000`), and `buildPreview` now renders a body that fits those bounds **in full**. So `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=1000` doesn't cap the model-visible output at ~1000 chars — a spilled body of 101–4000 chars still renders whole; the effective worst case is 4000 + header. Fine for gh-1604's "unsanitized 62K-line dumps" target, but the knob's doc ("a positive integer is the spill threshold in chars") reads as a hard cap.

Suggest one sentence on the env var's doc: *"the model-visible preview never exceeds the head+tail bounds (defaults: 4000 chars); thresholds below that floor change when spilling fires, not the preview's worst-case size."*

---

### Thread 7 — `test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: stale numbers in the test header comment**

The header says the default trigger on a 200k window "fires only at 183184" estimated tokens, but `CompactionSettings.forWindow(200000)` gives `reserveTokens = 16384` → trigger = 200000 − 16384 = **183616** (which is what `_defaultTrigger` on line 22 actually computes — the code is right, only the prose numbers are off, in both this line and line 20).

---

### Thread 8

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

**Summary**: One 🚨 BLOCKING bug — `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` throws an uncaught `ArgumentError` from `withCompactionTriggerTokens` (`int.clamp(1, 0)`), which propagates out of every compaction gate (run loop, resume boot cap, resume budget) and kills the run instead of degrading to defaults (reproduced against the packaged API). One ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override, contradicting the PR description, with no test pinning either precedence. Plus five 💡 suggestions (spills notes dropped on env override, faceless label for leading-newline commands, doc nits).

# pr-1612: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone ## Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1612._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/spill/spill.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: a command whose first line is empty renders a faceless label**

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

# pr-1612: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone ## Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

# pr-1612: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone ## Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
