project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). blocks.text:
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel. [#note,#source_agent,agent-loop,testing,gotcha,gh-1577]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness rework gotcha (gh-1403 round, 2026-10-08): the WIP auto-save bot formats staged Dart files with a PRE-tall-style formatter before committing — its commit fbf142951 reformatted ~1853 unrelated lines of test/release_hygiene_test.dart from the repo's canonical tall style (Dart 3.13 `dart format`, which CI's setup-dart stable produces and which main's files satisfy) into short style, silently bloating the PR diff even though CI itself does NOT gate on format (no `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml; only scripts/pre-commit self-heals, and only for agents that run it). Recovery recipe that worked: when a rework wants a test concern OUT of a god-file, checkout the file from origin/main (if the net intent is "file returns byte-identical to main") instead of incrementally un-deleting, rewrite any new sibling file with tall-style content, settle with `dart format`, and let the bot commit+push — never force-push over the automation. Verify the final `git diff origin/main --stat` is feature-shaped only. Also: the bot can race you between `git add` and `git commit` ("nothing to commit" = check `git log` — your tree is already committed/pushed; content identical means done). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually

Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

project: (note) flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length).
